title: Power Apps: Power Platform connectors in generative pages
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, licensing requirement and documented connector controls are supported. The data-policy path reaches the correct editor but stops before the connector classification action; this is a minor correction, not a publication blocker.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Makers can bring data from outside Dataverse into generative pages through Power Platform connectors.
claims.quote: Connector support lets a generative page use data outside of Dataverse through the Power Platform connector ecosystem.

claims.claim: Using a connector requires an existing created and authenticated connection.
claims.quote: If your page uses a Power Platform connector (preview), create and authenticate a connection.

claims.claim: The connector connection must have a connection reference in the environment.
claims.quote: Asks you to select a connection. If the connection doesn't have a connection reference, the agent creates one.

claims.claim: The maker selects connector data and describes how the page should use it.
claims.quote: select the prepared connection reference, and choose the connector data that the page should use. In your prompt, describe how you want the page to use the selected data.

claims.claim: Connector data can be incorporated in the page designer or through the generative pages AI plugin.
claims.quote: Connector data can be incorporated while working in the Maker Studio generative page designer or through the generative pages AI plugin.

claims.claim: Tools such as GitHub Copilot CLI can use the plugin to create connector-backed generative pages.
claims.quote: This article describes how to use AI code generation tools, such as GitHub Copilot CLI, to create and edit generative pages for model-driven apps in Power Apps.

claims.claim: Within the generative page designer, connector data is selected through Add data > Connectors.
claims.quote: To use data from a Power Platform connector (preview), select Add data > Connectors, select the prepared connection reference, and choose the connector data that the page should use.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: Learn currently describes connector support for generative pages as preview.
claims.quote: Connector support, Custom API support, and Application Insights telemetry for generative pages are preview features.

claims.claim: Connector-backed page operations depend on connection authorisation and permissions.
claims.quote: A method being present doesn't mean the page has a connector bound to it, or that the connection, dataset, table, or operation is configured, authorized, or permitted as expected.

claims.claim: SharePoint, SQL and SaaS systems are examples of external connector data sources.
claims.quote: The following are some of the enhanced connectors that use this pattern: ... SalesForce ... SharePoint ... SQL Server ... Zendesk

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: impact
claims.claim: A generated page can show connector data to app users.
claims.quote: For example, ask the agent to create a page that displays documents from a SharePoint list.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Generative page code is AI-generated.
claims.quote: the system then processes your requirements and specifications and intelligently generates React code that covers both the front-end user experience ... and the corresponding business logic.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises testing connector-backed pages with the identities and permissions users will have.
claims.quote: Review the connector data source in the plan before you approve the build. Test the generated page with the identities and permissions that your users will use.

claims.claim: A connection is a stored authentication credential for a connector.
claims.quote: A connection is a stored authentication credential for a connector, for example OAuth credentials for the SharePoint connector.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Connector methods can create rows in external connector tables.
claims.quote: createConnectorRow | Creates a new row in the specified connector table.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Connector methods can update rows in external connector tables.
claims.quote: updateConnectorRow | Updates an existing row in the specified connector table.

claims.claim: Connector methods can delete rows in connector tables.
claims.quote: deleteConnectorRow | Deletes a row from the specified connector table.

claims.claim: Connector calls reject their returned promise when the connection reference cannot be resolved.
claims.quote: connector methods reject the returned promise when a call fails — for example, when the connection reference can't be resolved

claims.claim: Connector calls reject when a connection is unauthorised and the user does not complete the consent prompt.
claims.quote: executeConnectorOperation resolves with ok: false for most error statuses, but still rejects for a missing operation, an unauthorized connection (403) without completed consent, or a transport failure.

claims.claim: Connection failures can interrupt page operations.
claims.quote: connector methods reject the returned promise when a call fails ... Wrap connector calls in try/catch.

claims.claim: The entitlement model is included within the premium use rights already required for model-driven apps.
claims.quote: Model-driven apps use Dataverse and are premium apps by default. Every user who runs a model-driven app needs a license that provides Power Apps premium use rights.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Every user who runs a model-driven app needs a licence providing Power Apps premium use rights.
claims.quote: Every user who runs a model-driven app needs a license that provides Power Apps premium use rights.

claims.claim: The Power Apps licensing FAQ lists premium connectors as features requiring premium entitlements.
claims.quote: Some examples of features that require premium entitlements include: premium connectors, Dataverse entities, on-premises data gateways, custom APIs, etc.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The licensing FAQ directs readers to the Power Platform Licensing Guide for qualifying licences.
claims.quote: For the complete and current list of qualifying licenses that provide premium Power Apps use rights, refer to the Microsoft Power Platform Licensing Guide.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing specific to connectors in generative pages is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: generative pages connectors licensing cost credits premium; Power Apps generative pages additional fees AI credits licensing. Read generative-pages, generative-page-external-tools and powerapps-licensing-faq; no separate licence for connector use in these pages.

claims.claim: Adding a premium connector does not by itself establish an additional purchase requirement beyond the app's existing premium rights.
claims.quote: Some examples of features that require premium entitlements include: premium connectors ... While Power Apps Premium ... satisfy the requirement generally, use rights differ by license and by the context the app runs in.

claims.claim: Connector use in generative pages is a maker-chosen capability, classified as user-opt-in.
claims.quote: To use data from a Power Platform connector (preview), select Add data > Connectors. Searched: generative pages admin enable disable environment setting Power Platform programmability API; read settings-features for generative settings; no connector-in-generative-pages switch documented.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Prebuilt connectors reaches connector classification.
claims.quote: select Security ... select Data and privacy ... select Data policy ... select New Policy to create a new policy to configure ... In the Prebuilt connectors section, select a Blockable connector
claims.fix: For connector blocking, extend the path to 'Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Prebuilt connectors > connector > Block'. Set its docs to https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/prevent-data-loss and cite that page. State in the row note that Block is available only for blockable connectors.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy creates a data policy from the supplied policy-definition object.
claims.quote: Creates a new DLP policy in the tenant by using the NewPolicy DLPPolicyDefinition object. ... New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy ... Creates a new policy with the $NewPolicy object.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: data policy paragraph
claims.claim: Platform data policies disable connections when the whole connector is blocked.
claims.quote: Scan connections. If the policy blocks the whole connector, set the connection to a disabled state so that it can't operate.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: data policy paragraph
claims.claim: Resources attempting to use inactive connections fail at runtime.
claims.quote: Any resources that are running and attempting to use an inactive connection, action, trigger, or MCP server that is blocked, fail at runtime.

claims.claim: A generative-page-specific data-policy enforcement sequence is not described beyond the documented platform process.
claims.quote: Searched: generative pages data policies enforcement connections. Opened generative-pages, generative-page-external-tools and wp-data-loss-prevention. The latter describes platform-wide enforcement; no separate designer/plugin generative-page sequence was found.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit policy > Prebuilt Connectors > connector > Configure connector > Connector endpoints reaches endpoint filtering.
claims.quote: The Endpoint configurable column on the Prebuilt Connectors page in Data Policies ... If ... Yes ... selecting Configure connector > Connector endpoints.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: New-PowerAppDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations with TenantId, PolicyName and NewDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations creates endpoint-filtering configurations.
claims.quote: New-PowerAppDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations -TenantId $TenantId -PolicyName $PolicyName -NewDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations $ConnectorConfigurations

claims.claim: Connector endpoint filtering is a preview platform control available for supported connectors.
claims.quote: Connector endpoint filtering (preview) ... It's configured within a data policy, and it's exclusively available for the following connectors:

claims.claim: Endpoint filtering evaluates static endpoints known and selected at design time.
claims.quote: Only static endpoints that are known and selected when building an app, flow, or chatbot during design time are enforced.

claims.claim: Endpoint-filtering rules do not apply to environment variables, custom inputs or dynamically bound runtime endpoints.
claims.quote: Endpoint filtering rules aren't enforced on environment variables, custom inputs, and dynamically bound endpoints during runtime.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls: third table row
claims.claim: Power Apps > Solutions > solution > New > More > Connection Reference opens connection-reference creation.
claims.quote: Sign in to Power Apps ... select Solutions ... Create a new or open an existing solution ... select New > More > Connection Reference.

claims.where: controls[2].api; controls[2].note; Governance controls: third table row
claims.claim: PATCH [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/connectionreferences(<connectionreferenceid>) updates a connection-reference row.
claims.quote: Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/connectionreferences ... Primary key: connectionreferenceid ... Operations supported: POSTGETPATCHDELETE

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls: third table row
claims.claim: The connection-reference update uses connectionid to specify the connection's API hub ID.
claims.quote: connectionid | Edm.String | Id of the connection in API hub ... Display name: Connection Id

claims.claim: The generative pages prerequisites direct makers to create the reference in Solutions > Default Solution.
claims.quote: Then open Solutions > Default Solution and create a connection reference that uses the connection.

claims.claim: A connection reference is a solution component pointing to a connection.
claims.quote: A connection reference is a solution component that contains a reference to a connection about a specific connector.

claims.claim: During solution import, a connection is provided for each connection reference in the target environment.
claims.quote: During solution import into a target environment, a connection is provided for all the connection references

claims.where: controls[3].ui; controls[3].api; Governance controls: fourth table row
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no UI or API switch specific to connectors in generative pages.
claims.quote: Searched: generative pages connectors disable admin PowerShell API setting; Power Apps generative pages admin enable disable environment setting Power Platform programmability API. Read generative-pages, generative-page-external-tools, settings-features and PAC model excerpts; no specific switch.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Connection references have owners that administrators can review.
claims.quote: _ownerid_value | ownerid | Owner Id ... _owninguser_value | owninguser | Unique identifier for the user that owns the record.

claims.claim: Connector action control restricts individual actions within a permitted connector.
claims.quote: You can use connector action control to allow or block individual actions or triggers within a given connector.
